posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Imbued Fire would never effect a hero through Isolated Hero, because that is a hero card directly affecting another hero.  The affect of the card is to increase fire damage by 1, if the damage being increased is the effect of a hero card, then the interaction cannot occur.  If the damage being increased is the effect of a non-hero card than it can be increased.

Imbued Fire's boost to fire damage would however make an environment or villain card that deals fire damage deal +1 damage.  Whether that villain deals that damage to a hero or not would not matter, it gets the bonus.  If a hero is the target of that damage the hero is in no way causing or being affected by the affect of imbued fire, since they are not dealing damage their damage can't be boosted.  The villain card effect is being affected.

 

 

By any means would not work because while By any Means is affecting the villain, the effect does affect a hero card effect.  The hero deals damage, the damage is a Hero Card Effect, it cannot be increased by a hero card effect through Isolated hero.

Twist the Ether on a villain would work because damage dealt by a villain is a villain card effect, and Twist the Ether can affect a villain card effect through Isolated Hero.

 

Summary:

1.  Imbued Fire's increase of fire damage could not affect damage caused by a hero card effect or dealt by a hero, but could increase damage dealt to a hero by a non-hero card effect.

2.  By any Means is a Hero card, and cannot affect the effect of a hero card through Isolated Hero, therefore it cannot increase damage that is dealt by a hero or hero card effect.

3.  Twist the Ether could affect damage dealt by a non-hero target by a non-hero card effect.

 

Rational:

1.  Damage is the effect of the both the dealer of the damage, and the card that causes it to be dealt.

2.  Taking damage is not an effect, but the result of an effect of the card and dealer of the damage.

3.  The wording of Isolated Hero stops interaction between Heroes, their cards and card effects.

 

Interesting things: (my answer)

1.  Take Down is a hero card causing a villain to deal damage, could it be affected by Twist the Ether?  (No, the damage is a hero card effect)

2.  Infection is a Villain Card causing a hero to deal damage, could it be affected by a hero card?  (I would guess no, since a hero is dealing the damage)

posts.name: jagarciao
posts.cooked:
It can also be argued that when you increase damage dealt to a target you are affecting only that target's interaction with the damage and not the sender's. Whereas "damage dealt by" has the opposite interaction. 
 
Basically, a damage dealer puts out a "package" of damage, the value of which package is based on the active effects that are in play that are affecting the damage dealer. When this damage "package" reaches a target, it is then also modified by whatever active effects are in play affecting the target. Any card limiting interactions between hero effects and Isolated Heroes would only limit the part of the interaction that corresponds to the Isolated Hero. 
 
Is this interpretation correct? I don't know... there hasn't been a precedent set because the nuances of the interaction don't ever come into play until Isolated Hero... quite honestly this isn't even the view I take when I look at the card's effect, but there is an amount of logic behind that that we shouldn't really deny because it doesn't match out view... But we seem to always get hung up on why "my interpretation is right and yours is wrong" that we fail to see that both of them are entirely plausible. we just argue and argue ad nauseam on how "backwards" the other theories are and how "absurd" people can be for even entertaining the possibility that such a "ridiculous" idea can even be conceived as being correct. 
The funniest part of all this is that the final answer will not be settled by the most "logical" answer or the one with the best explanation... It'll be whatever interpretation Christopher had in mind when he crated the card or when he makes his ruling. And then we'll just accept it and move on... even though just a post or two before we were nearly spewing vitriol at each other over it.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked: Isolated Hero is meant to stop effects that specifically target other heroes and their cards. HP regain, damage increases (Increase damage dealt BY HEROES), destroy their ongoing cards, etc. and vice-versa. It is not intended -- nor can it logically be interpreted -- to affect any INDIRECT interactions, like increasing damage dealt TO villain targets (because it targets the villains, not the heroes), destroying villain cards that affect hero cards, destroying environment cards, dealing damage to any non-hero cards, etc. Because of the way By Any Means is written, it doesn't affect the hero at all, and it doesn't boost the hero's damage; rather, it just says "oh, this villain is taking damage? increase it!"

I am Rabk, candidate for Isolated Hero, and I endorse this opinion. 

It took some work to get there, but I'm 100% with Phantaskippy and Foote now that they've settled their differences. 

 

Still not fully addressed, however, is Stun Bolt/Ground Pound/Hypersonic Assault. I move that their effects should still work, regardless of isolated status. I'm honestly too lazy to attempt a rule-based justification and will instead just say that it makes sense from a story-telling perspective. The Wraith catches an "Old Lady" in the Street - she punches her in the throat, shoots her, and then moves on to her next victim (Maia apparently missed out on the whole Boy Scout thing…). If a lost and confused Bunker walks by a few minutes later (i.e., the next villain turn), would the Old Lady suddenly forget about her mutilated larynx and be able to attack him simply because he's all alone? I would say no. I hear the argument about different time periods or timelines and the possibility that Bunker is isolated somewhere/somewhen else entirely, but I can't make sense of it thematically. Did he encounter a completely different Old Lady, one who is somehow not experiencing any shortness of breath? Then why is her HP reduced just as is she had been throat-jabbed and submitted her to a certain degree of nonconsensual projectile-violation?

True, the effect that is protecting Bunker ultimately originated with Wraith, but since the villain card acts as an intermediary it does not effect the isolated hero directly. This is the same logic chain that argues for Imbue Fire increasing the fire damage a volcano deals to an isolated hero: in both cases the effect acts through an intermediary, non-hero card.

 

 

[Edit: To expand on someone's earlier statement regarding By Any Means, the bounty says to increase damage dealt to the target. Thematically, Jim's telling his team that the target needs to be eliminated "by any means" neccesary. By putting a bounty on her head he is urging the other heroes to attack more aggresively. (I know it has nothing to do with rules, but the flavor text also seems to pretty much insist that this particular bounty interacts with other heroes.) If the card instead said to increase damage taken by the target, I could better see the argument for allowing interaction with isolated heroes. Maybe he threw sand in her eyes or pants'ed her or something to take her off her guard and reduce her defenses. (We'd have to rename the card, though - maybe "Kick 'em while They're Down"?  )

Yes, I realize the analogy's not perfect since environment damage is also increased, but I do my best. Maybe "By Any Means" is in fact a big green holographic Bounty Beacon[sup]®[/sup] that makes it easier for everyone (even velocirapotors!) to see the target?  ]
